title: OpenChainGraph third-party kernel submitter identity
description: Shape of submitter.json, one per submitter directory under ocg-conformance/third-party/<submitter-slug>/. Binds a submission to a verified GitHub identity and derives a reverse-DNS-style namespace from it (2026 enhancement, modelled on the MCP Registry reference: namespace/identity binding via verified accounts). This file identifies WHO submitted the vectors in the sibling manifest.json; it makes no claim about the kernel's correctness -- see trust_disclaimer.

name.description: Human or organization display name of the submitter.

contact_url.description: A dereferenceable contact URL for the submitter (homepage, issue tracker, or an email-as-URI mailto: link).

submitted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the submission PR.

github_identity.description: Verified GitHub identity binding. The minimum bar (verification_method: github-pr-author) is the submission PR's own author field -- GitHub records who opened a PR independent of the file content, so a submitter cannot claim someone else's account without controlling it. Stronger methods are allowed but not required.

username.description: GitHub login, no leading @, matching GitHub's own username character rules.

profile_url.description: Must be https://github.com/<username> for the same username above -- a structural cross-check, not just free text.

verification_method.description: How control of the identity was established. github-pr-author: the submission PR was opened from this GitHub account (default, zero extra ceremony). github-oauth-app: submitter authorized a first-party OAuth app that asserted the account. dns-txt-record: submitter proved control of the namespace directly via DNS, independent of GitHub (only meaningful when namespace is not under io.github.*).

namespace.description: Reverse-DNS-style namespace for this submitter's kernel ids, mirroring the MCP Registry io.github.* convention. MUST equal io.github.<github_identity.username> (lowercased) when verification_method is github-pr-author or github-oauth-app. A dns-txt-record verification may use any reverse-DNS namespace the submitter proved ownership of by other means. Every vector id in the sibling manifest.json must start with this namespace plus a literal dot (checked by validate-submission.mjs and, later, by the USERKERNEL-CI-1 Action -- not encodable as a single-file JSON Schema constraint since it is a cross-field, cross-file rule).

trust_disclaimer.const: Conformance-suite-pass is not a correctness guarantee, not an endorsement, and not an audit. AINumbers verifies formats; it does not verify facts.
trust_disclaimer.description: Verbatim liability-boundary line (USERKERNEL-CONFORMANCE-BUILD-SPEC.md section 3.4). A JSON Schema const forces byte-identical text so this cannot drift per-submitter -- the whole point is that it always reads the same regardless of who is submitting.
